title: Development and Evaluation of the Altruistic Orientation Towards Strangers Scale (AOTS)
abstract: Abstract: Trait altruism reflects a tendency to engage in voluntary behavior that benefits others, with personal cost in terms of time, resources, and/or effort, and without expectation of direct reward. Current measures of altruism focus on assessing the frequency of engaging in prosocial behaviors assumed to be altruistically motivated. To address this limitation, we developed the Altruistic Orientation Towards Strangers (AOTS) scale following a review of the literature and identification of key elements of altruism. In exploratory studies, the AOTS was developed using data from three convenience samples, including students at a large Canadian university (Sample 1: N = 1,295), Prolific users in Canada and the United States (Sample 2: N = 302), and Prolific users in the United Kingdom (Sample 3: N = 297). After addressing a volunteering factor and negative-wording nuisance factor, exploratory factor analysis suggested a one-factor structure. Scores on the final AOTS were significantly correlated with related traits and demonstrated criterion-related validity with prosocial outcomes, including COVID-19 behaviors (Samples 1–2) and generosity (Samples 1–3). These results provide preliminary evidence for the AOTS as a new measure of altruistic tendencies toward strangers; however, additional research is needed to evaluate discriminant validity and explore other prosocial outcomes.
